title: DNA Extraction from Zooplankton Samples
author: coline.royaux
materials: Briefly centrifuge to remove drops from the lid.

steps.title: Label and arrange tubes
steps.instruction: Prepare 50 tubes (or a 50‑well plate) with one individual per well and alternate genus between wells to allow detection of cross‑contamination.

steps.title: Collect and record specimen
steps.instruction: Collect one individual from the sample, note its genus and determine its sex using a binocular microscope.

steps.title: Place specimen in tube and dry
steps.instruction: For individuals >5 mm dissect a few legs, place the legs in the well and the remaining body in a tagged Eppendorf tube; for individuals ≤5 mm place the whole body in the well. If needed, add alcohol to let the material settle, then allow the biological material to dry. Use a micropipette to remove any excess alcohol and keep the plate closed for transport.

steps.title: Add ATL buffer and equilibrate
steps.instruction: Add 180 µL ATL buffer to each well and let the mixture equilibrate to room temperature.

steps.title: Incubate for lysis
steps.instruction: Place the tubes in a proofer at 56 °C overnight (minimum 6 hours) to lyse the tissues.

steps.title: Set batch size for manual extraction
steps.instruction: When performing the manual DNA extraction, process at most 20 tubes at a time because the timing between steps is short.

steps.title: Add AL buffer and vortex
steps.instruction: Add 200 µL AL buffer (include RNase if desired) to each tube and mix by pulse‑vortexing for 15 seconds.

steps.title: Wash column with AW1 buffer
steps.instruction: Transfer the lysate to a spin column, add 500 µL AW1 buffer, centrifuge at 8000 rpm, temperature °C, for 1 minute; discard the collection tube containing the flow‑through and place the column in a clean 2 mL collection tube.

steps.title: Wash column with AW2 buffer
steps.instruction: Add 500 µL AW2 buffer to the column, centrifuge at 8000 rpm, temperature °C, for 1 minute; discard the collection tube containing the flow‑through and place the column in a clean 2 mL collection tube.

steps.title: Dry membrane
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at full speed (rpm not specified), temperature °C, for 3 minutes to dry the membrane completely.

steps.title: Add proteinase K
steps.instruction: Add 20 µL proteinase K to each well, pulse‑vortex for 15 seconds and briefly centrifuge.

steps.title: Add ethanol and incubate
steps.instruction: Add 200 µL 96‑100 % ethanol to each tube, pulse‑vortex for 15 seconds, then incubate at room temperature for 5 minutes.

steps.title: Prepare optional RNA carrier
steps.instruction: If an RNA carrier is required, for 20 tubes (use 22 volumes to avoid error) dissolve 22 µg solid RNA carrier in 22 µL AE buffer; then mix 22 µL of this AE + RNAse solution with 4400 µL AL buffer (200 µL per volume) and mix thoroughly.

steps.title: Prepare elution columns
steps.instruction: Place each elution column into a clean 2 mL collection tube.

steps.title: Transfer lysate to column and spin
steps.instruction: Pipette the prepared DNA lysate onto the column, centrifuge at 8000 rpm, temperature °C, for 1 minute; discard the collection tube containing the flow‑through and keep the column in a clean 2 mL tube. Ensure the column is empty; if liquid remains, centrifuge at a higher speed until empty.

steps.title: Elute DNA with AE buffer
steps.instruction: Add 50 µL AE buffer to the column, incubate at room temperature for 1 minute, then centrifuge at full speed (rpm not specified), temperature °C, for 1 minute. The DNA eluate is now in the clean Eppendorf tube; discard the column.
